findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks sender
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every active `Integration` has a `sender` object with a `login`. Integrations created before this change, and first-time installs where the installation webhook has not populated `state["sender"]`, do not have `metadata["sender"]` (see `build_integration`, which only adds it when `state.get("sender")` is truthy). When such an `Integration` exists but no `OrganizationIntegration` is attached to the current org, this path raises `KeyError` and returns a 500 instead of the intended GitHub installation failure page, breaking legitimate reinstallation or linking. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and explicitly handle the missing-sender case.

findings.title: GitHub user validation is skipped for first-time installs
findings.body: When `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately, before the `github_authenticated_user` vs `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` comparison at lines 500-505. `build_integration` also only records `sender` if it was already present in pipeline state, so a normal first installation creates an integration with no sender metadata. Consequently, the PR's stated protection against an OAuth-authenticated GitHub user differing from the installing GitHub user is not enforced on the initial installation; it only applies once an `Integration` object already exists (usually via a webhook). An attacker can exploit the race or the normal first-install path where the webhook has not created/populated the integration before pipeline completion.

findings.title: get_user_info errors are not handled and can crash install
findings.body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is called outside the surrounding `try`/`except` that handles token-response parsing failures. `get_user_info` makes a GitHub API request and can raise `ApiError` on invalid tokens, rate limits, or network failures; similarly, `safe_urlopen` for the token exchange on line 423 is before the `try` block and can raise on connection failures. These exceptions propagate as a 500 instead of rendering the advertised `github-integration-failed` error page, contradicting the PR's goal of failing gracefully when GitHub authentication cannot be validated.
